title: Legitimate broader parent emerges later and triggers possible reparenting

objects.title: V2 Incremental Reliability
objects.persistentConcern: Ensuring incremental semantic updates are durable, ordered, recoverable, and not lost.

objects.title: V2 Incremental Performance
objects.persistentConcern: Reducing latency and unnecessary computation in incremental semantic updates.

newMessages.content: I think we're making a mistake by treating the reliability and performance work as completely separate implementation tasks now. Before Kiro changes either one again, I want us to step back and define what the V2 incremental engine itself is supposed to guarantee end to end—how a message moves from persistence through semantic processing, mutation generation, commit, recovery, and eventually performance optimization. I want the whole incremental engine architecture to be something we can reason about as one system.
So rather than only discussing reliability or latency independently, you want an explicit system-level architecture for the incremental engine itself.
Exactly. Reliability and performance should still remain separate concerns inside it, but I want the engine architecture itself to become something we can return to and design.

semanticPacket.conciseMeaning: The user establishes the V2 Incremental Engine itself as a persistent system-level architecture concern encompassing the end-to-end update lifecycle while retaining reliability and performance as distinct internal concerns.
